diagrams.title: From Fragmented Listings to a Firm Max Bid
diagrams.subtitle: The five-step loop practitioners run before any government surplus bid

stages.label: Map the platforms
stages.detail: Delaware, New Castle County, and Wilmington each sold through a different platform; GSA Auctions, GovDeals, Public Surplus, and Municibid are the core channels, with no dealer license required.

stages.label: Pull historical sold prices
stages.detail: Search US Gov Bid past auctions going back years to see what everything sold for before setting a max.

stages.label: Read the terms of sale
stages.detail: Payment method and deadline, a GovDeals buyer's premium of 5% to 12.5%, the pickup window, and title versus bill of sale.

stages.label: Inspect or send an inspector
stages.detail: Walk from poke-through frame rust, flood signs, or a mismatched VIN; if inspection day is impossible, hire a mobile ASE-certified inspection service where the yard allows it.

stages.label: Set a firm max bid and hold it
stages.detail: Price in sales tax, buyer's premiums, and shipping, then write the number down; if bidding passes it, let it go.

diagrams.caption: Keyed vehicles at Norfolk government auctions had a $1,300 middle price versus $550 without keys, and Public Surplus caps card purchases at $4,000, so the terms decide the real price.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All figures are attributed practitioner claims; premiums are set by each selling municipality and vary by listing.
diagrams.note: Attributed to East Coast Classics (q09PUtJPIxs), UX Auctions (Z87d62pWVEk), GovAuctions (Ie7zxVOXjeE), and The Salmon Runs (jaeWKn_Nu68).

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before a GovPlanet Humvee Bid
diagrams.subtitle: Engine health, walk-away number, clearance wait, and paperwork

nodes.question: Does the start clip show a first-crank fire, smooth idle, and no blow-by mist from the radiator cap?
nodes.fail_action: Kill the listing; a healthy truck costs no more at auction.

nodes.question: Is the walk-away number written down before the auction closes?
nodes.fail_action: Do not bid; 30-second overtime extensions pushed one win from $9,500 to $12,500.

nodes.question: Can you wait up to 12 weeks for end-use clearance and hit the seven-day pickup window?
nodes.fail_action: Pass; daily storage charges start once the pickup window closes.

nodes.question: Will your DMV accept the SF-97 paperwork and will an insurer take the six-digit serial?
nodes.pass_next: Bid, budgeting invoice fees and broker shipping of $500 to $1,200 by distance.
nodes.fail_action: Hold off until the DMV and an insurer both confirm.

diagrams.caption: A $10,200 win invoiced at $12,290.40 after a $1,030 transaction fee and a $50 SF-97 fee, and broker shipping ran $850 from Albany, Georgia to St. Louis, Missouri.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Gate order is an organizing sequence; each gate condition and dollar figure is an attributed practitioner claim.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Kevin24Seven (gtS8l93r5cw, F0AkAibFp2g, gXjTPh7cGHU), Split Builds (CkfJvTDwa2w), and Rattlesnake Defense (WzbjxUJRWKI).

diagrams.title: The Reseller Tax Setup
diagrams.subtitle: One seller's permit at the hub, certificates and filings on every spoke

center.focus: Collect and remit sales tax, and buy inventory tax-free so the tax lands once, on the end consumer.

spokes.role: Florida Department of Revenue (DR-1 and DR-13)
spokes.kpi: DR-13 pushed to every vendor before December 31; quarterly return filed even at zero in-state sales
35 of 45 sales-tax states covered; about 10 states require registration
About 50 printed certificate copies a year; yes-list retailers only
Tax due plus 10% of the tax or $500, whichever is more, per misused purchase

diagrams.caption: Skipping the certificate means paying $70,000 on $1,000,000 of inventory at 7%; in Florida, wholesale buys run 7% to 7.5% once county surtax is added.
diagrams.assumptions_note: State rules shown are the practitioners' reported examples for Florida and California and vary by state.
diagrams.note: Attributed to James Baker CPA (CiHy9lcx3x4, L4NQWUrzH6A), Santiago Cueto (K5oBesJVonE), LedgerGurus (It-VnUi3x58), Lester John (7J3W8esngfU), Jack Hagwell (iNfW7YXuTOA), and Matt Sokol Business (vwdB1U0_hGs).

diagrams.title: Contracts and Claims: The File Wins
diagrams.subtitle: Reading, pricing, answering, and documenting DLA awards and tax-free sales

weeks.title: Decode the solicitation
weeks.deliverable: PR number read: 1-0-0 means an estimated IDC quantity, 700 or 090 means a firm quantity you must supply
weeks.gate: Quote only once the quantity type and inspection boxes are confirmed

weeks.title: Price the bid
weeks.deliverable: Vendor cost, packaging, and inspection rolled into a 10% to 15% margin
weeks.gate: Drop 20% to 25% margins, which get underbid

weeks.title: Answer traceability and counteroffers
weeks.deliverable: Re-confirmed vendor price, PDF documents on the original thread, and an Excel informal cost breakdown (6.75% profit, $261 per unit on 195 pieces)
weeks.gate: Refuse a counteroffer when the math does not work

weeks.title: Lock the tax and claim file
weeks.deliverable: Complete, signed, dated certificates; Texas production within 90 days of notice; a $4 grant deed for surplus-fund claims
weeks.gate: No tax-free release without a certificate matching what the customer buys

diagrams.caption: Traceability requests, counteroffers, and cost-breakdown requests signal an award is close; MeND has refused government counteroffers and still won.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The four-week sequence is an organizing frame, not a schedule any practitioner stated; all thresholds and dollar figures are attributed claims.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Tris10 @ MeND (sG-wAF0b7kQ, Y895jCYSE5A), Secureframe (v7nJCLRc0uo), Tax Expert Today (WZL5m9rfNSQ), and Overage Acquisition (X_Oq8vv4j_c).
